title: Measuring Verifier Impact in an LLM Generate→Verify→Repair Loop for Intent→Configuration NetOps Tasks
abstract: We measure how inserting a deterministic network verifier into a generate→verify→repair loop changes verifier-detected safety violations of LLM-produced device-configuration proposals. In a preregistered paired design (N=500 intent→configuration tasks) we compared (1) baseline: a single LLM proposal (gpt-5-mini) and (2) guarded: the same LLM proposal screened by a deterministic netops validator with up to one automated repair iteration. Primary outcome: verifier pass (no preregistered high/medium-severity violations). Results (complete pairs = 500): baseline passed 499/500 (0.998), guarded passed 500/500 (1.000); absolute paired success-rate difference = 0.002; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00; paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.006]. The preregistered generation_semantics = 'shared_initial_candidate' means the same initial model proposal was evaluated under both arms and repair was invoked only when the validator flagged that shared candidate. On this synthetic, verifier-scoped corpus and this model+validator pairing the LLM produced near-ceiling proposals, so the marginal measured verifier+repair effect on the pass-rate metric is numerically small. All preregistration, execution, prompts, outputs, and validator traces are archived in the evidence bundle (representative artifact: execution/raw_results.jsonl, SHA-256 = e7c1fc4d8932389dc3e4c651cf6db08a84ba3a1cd4893b9d7d985618929ff945).

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed for NetOps tasks such as intent→configuration translation, change planning, and limited automated repair. Prior work emphasizes that operational reliability depends on surrounding engineering—deterministic validators, sandbox replay, canarying, and rollback mechanisms—rather than on the model alone [Beckett et al., 2017; Wei et al., 2025; Bilal et al., 2026]. Generate→verify→repair patterns are a common mitigation, but controlled measurements that isolate the verifier’s contribution are scarce. We preregistered and executed a paired experiment to answer a focused operational question: how much does integrating a deterministic network verifier into a generate→verify→repair loop reduce verifier-detected safety violations in LLM-generated device-configuration proposals, compared to LLM-only proposals, when tasks and topologies are canonical and restricted to verifier-modeled features? We report the preregistered design, artifact-backed execution, confirmatory analysis, and interpretation boundaries.
sections.related_work: Deterministic and formal network-verification methods (header-space and route-model verifiers) can check reachability, isolation, and update-safety on configuration models [Beckett et al., 2017]. Recent NetOps/AIOps systems integrate LLMs into intent-driven pipelines and emphasize validators and guardrails as essential for safe automation [Wei et al., 2025; Bilal et al., 2026]. Generate–verify–repair and verifier-assisted self-correction have been studied in structured-generation domains, but published controlled ablations that quantify verifier effect size in LLM-driven NetOps pipelines are limited [INTA, 2025; Confucius, 2025]. Failure-mode analyses of LLM applications (hallucination, overconfidence, tool failures) further motivate guardrails [Owen, 2026]. Our contribution is an artifact-backed, preregistered paired measurement that isolates verifier+repair impact under constrained synthetic conditions.
sections.methodology: Design and preregistration: The study was preregistered (study_id cand_7f4b9a2d_hosted_gvr_v1_2026) before execution. Confirmatory hypothesis: an LLM paired with a deterministic verifier plus one automated repair iteration will produce a lower verifier-detected safety-violation rate than the same LLM producing a single proposal without verifier feedback (paired, within-task). Sampling and tasks: 500 deterministic synthetic intent→configuration tasks were generated deterministically and stratified across three canonical clusters as preregistered: VLAN-change = 167 tasks, ACL-change = 167 tasks, static-route-change = 166 tasks (the preregistered allocation placed the remainder deterministically by seed). No confirmatory exclusions occurred. Models, validator, and orchestration: LLM = gpt-5-mini (provider recorded as openai_responses) called via the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter; deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Generation semantics: preregistered generation_semantics = 'shared_initial_candidate' with independent_condition_generation = false. For each task the pipeline produced one shared LLM proposal that served as the baseline output and was also evaluated by the guarded arm; a guarded repair call was issued only when the validator flagged a preregistered high/medium-severity violation on that shared candidate. This isolates verifier+repair effect conditional on the identical initial model proposal rather than measuring verifier-guided regeneration or repeated-generation strategies. Primary estimand and analysis: primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Primary test = exact McNemar two-sided (alpha = 0.05); paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (B = 10000, seed = 1729). The analysis executor was paired_binary_analysis_v1. Missingness, exclusions, retries, stopping rules, and sensitivity treatments followed the preregistration and are recorded in the execution manifest.
sections.results: Execution and accounting: completed pairs = 500; model_calls_used = 501; provider-audit stage_counts recorded shared_initial_generation = 500 and repair = 1 (deterministic_reconciliation provider_call_audit; deterministic_reconciliation.json SHA-256 = ab00aaa4ef0f3a93667b9ce281c2673e51ff5f72fc6a050d264221addfafdd00). Primary confirmatory outcomes: baseline_success_count = 499 (baseline_success_rate = 0.998); guarded_success_count = 500 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). Paired contingency: n11 = 499, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 59083229020449533f326d8813067d527b64b36dd1e8a91badfcd68fa0a3867c). Absolute paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0020000000000000018. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00; paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.006] (analysis_log.jsonl SHA-256 = 41f5e410f3da00fdb0258a3b5240767356a67b8d741502abe6af2396d21f88e2). Why p = 1.00: the analysis executor implements the exact McNemar two-sided test as the two-sided binomial test on discordant pairs (n = n10 + n01); with n = 1 and observed k = 1 in one discordant cell the two-sided exact binomial p-value as computed in the archived analysis_log.jsonl equals 1.00 under the chosen two-sided convention—this arithmetic and implementation are recorded in the analysis artifact. Repair activity and discordant-pair provenance: zero tasks were excluded for unmodeled features; observed repair-stage provider calls = 1. The single discordant pair (the one task where the guarded arm corrected a baseline-detected violation) is present in the archived per-task raw results. Retrieval instruction and archival identifiers: the full per-task records (shared candidate, baseline and guarded scorer results, validator traces, and provider-call traces) are archived in execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 = e7c1fc4d8932389dc3e4c651cf6db08a84ba3a1cd4893b9d7d985618929ff945). To locate the discordant pair unambiguously, search execution/raw_results.jsonl for pair_id entries where the baseline scoring outcome indicates a verifier-detected high/medium-severity violation (baseline pass==0) while the guarded outcome for the same pair_id indicates pass==1; because only one such discordant pair exists in the confirmatory set, this lookup returns the single episode and its provider-call traces. The repair-stage provider-call trace referenced by that per-task record is archived among the provider-call artifacts referenced in the execution manifest. Representative per-task exemplar files and artifact hashes are recorded in the manuscript evidence bundle.
sections.discussion: On this synthetic, verifier-scoped corpus and with the tested model+validator pairing the LLM produced near-ceiling correct proposals (499/500 baseline passes). Consequently the measured marginal verifier+repair benefit on the pass-rate metric is numerically small (absolute improvement 0.002) and inference is limited by a ceiling effect. Nonetheless the observed discordant case shows that a verifier+repair loop can correct at least some rare baseline failures. Operational interpretation depends strongly on baseline error prevalence and verifier modeling coverage: in distributions with higher baseline error rates or broader verifier coverage, verifier+repair gains on safety metrics are expected to be larger. The preregistered shared_initial_candidate design intentionally isolates the verifier+repair effect conditional on the same initial candidate and therefore does not measure potential gains from verifier-guided regeneration or larger repair budgets; different generation/regeneration semantics or larger repair budgets would address distinct operational questions. Our artifacts permit inspection of the corrected instance, the validator-detected violation codes, and the repair-stage trace for qualitative failure-mode analysis (see retrieval instruction above).
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment (N=500) comparing an LLM-only pipeline to an LLM plus deterministic verifier with one automated repair iteration under shared-initial-generation semantics. Both arms achieved near-perfect verifier pass rates (baseline 499/500, guarded 500/500), producing an absolute improvement of 0.002 (95% CI [0.0, 0.006]; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00). The result quantifies a ceiling-effect regime where an already-accurate LLM leaves limited measured marginal utility for a verifier on the pass-rate metric; it does not imply verifiers are unnecessary in broader, noisier, or cross-vendor production settings. Practitioners should measure proposal error prevalence and verifier coverage on realistic workloads to prioritize guardrail investments. All preregistration, execution, prompt, output, and validator artifacts are archived and hashed in the evidence bundle for independent verification (representative artifact: execution/raw_results.jsonl, SHA-256 = e7c1fc4d8932389dc3e4c651cf6db08a84ba3a1cd4893b9d7d985618929ff945).

limitations: Synthetic, deterministic task corpus limited to features modeled by the deterministic validator; results do not necessarily generalize to unconstrained production intents, cross-vendor CLI heterogeneity, or protocol semantics outside the verifier scope. Representative task payloads show allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}.
Single model family tested (gpt-5-mini) — no claim of multi-model generality is made.
Maximum one automated repair iteration was permitted; different repair budgets or iterative regeneration strategies may change measured verifier impact.

Very high baseline pass rate (499/500) creates a ceiling effect that limits power to detect small absolute improvements on the pass-rate metric; the observed non-significant exact McNemar p = 1.00 should be interpreted in that context rather than as evidence that verifiers are universally unnecessary.
